agree.reason: The all-or-nothing promise and the lower goal reassure a reader who remembers the refunds, but saying 'you need $13,000 more than last time' while leaving out the $11,000 already pledged and the spending reports gives a reader who just gave to the ambulance fund little reason to pledge much.

honest.reason: Most claims track the facts, but 'the lights come back on this Thanksgiving' turns a plan into a promise, and calling the bank's 29% 'a quarter' undersells it slightly.

works_the_facts.reason: The 76-mile round trip and the $60,000 public share are worked out well, but the draft frames the gap as $13,000 more than last time when the $11,000 in written business pledges would leave only $49,000, just $2,000 above last time's total, and it never puts the ask in per-household terms.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is shown accurately as no screen in town and a 76-mile round trip, set against a lease on offer now, though it doesn't spell out that the $1 lease and the bank pledge both go away if the goal is missed.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing condition is checkable, with a date, an amount and a consequence, but the roof estimate that could rise by up to 15% is left out, and Thanksgiving carries no hedge.

objections.reason: The worry about another failed campaign is answered, but the trust objection goes without the quarterly spending report, the draft raises its own 'more than last time' objection that the $11,000 already answers, and the pull of competing local causes is never addressed.

fit.reason: It is a signed, clearly sectioned crowdfunding pitch, well under 350 words.
